::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
## Status: design. No probe has run.

Written against [the design standard](../studies/DESIGN-STANDARD.md). Shares its case
definitions and reason mapping with [P17](P17-fast-acceptance-and-retraction.qmd).
:::

## 1. The question

An ORCID identifier that a publisher has authenticated ties a byline to a person who logged in to
claim it. A paper mill selling authorship slots, or inventing authors, has less reason to produce
that link. The share of a paper's authors carrying an authenticated ORCID is therefore a
candidate integrity signal that is cheap to compute for every article ever published.

## 2. Prior work, and the search behind the novelty claim

Log key `P18`.

```
corpus regex: ORCID.{0,80}(retract|misconduct|integrity|paper mill)
PubMed:       ORCID[tiab] AND (retract*[tiab] OR "paper mill*"[tiab]
              OR misconduct[tiab] OR "research integrity"[tiab])
```

Seven PubMed records, none in the corpus. The closest proposes recording retractions on ORCID
profiles (PMID 38815635); another discusses author name ambiguity (PMID 38704656). None measures
ORCID coverage as a marker of retraction risk.

## 3. Hypothesis

Articles retracted for misconduct-class reasons have a smaller share of authors with an
authenticated ORCID than matched controls; articles retracted for honest error do not.

**Null.** The odds ratio per 10-point increase in authenticated share is 1 for misconduct cases.

**What would falsify it.** No association for misconduct, or an equal association for honest
error, which would point to journal-level practice rather than to fraud.

## 4. Design and unit

Matched case-control, run separately for the two reason classes, as in P17.

## 5. Sample

Cases and reason classes as defined in P17, from Retraction Watch with a DOI, published 2016 or
later, when publisher ORCID deposit to Crossref became common. Controls: four per case, same
journal and publication month, not in Retraction Watch (S9).

## 6. Exposure

The share of an article's authors whose Crossref author record carries an ORCID with
`authenticated-orcid` true. OpenAlex attaches ORCIDs by inference as well as from publisher
deposit, and an inferred ORCID says nothing about whether the author claimed the paper, so
OpenAlex is used only for a sensitivity analysis and never for the primary exposure (S3).

## 7. Outcome

Case or control status, by reason class.

## 8. Validation gate

The reason mapping is validated in P17. Here, the author checks for 100 articles that the
Crossref record's authenticated ORCIDs match the ORCIDs printed on the publisher page.
**Below 95 percent agreement, the exposure is recomputed from the source that agrees with the
article.**

## 9. Analysis

In R.

```r
clogit(case ~ I(auth_share * 10) + log(n_authors) + strata(match_set), data = d)
```

Fitted per reason class. Author count enters because a single-author paper has a share of 0 or 1
and large teams have intermediate shares for reasons unrelated to fraud.

## 10. Threats

| threat | handling | removed or disclosed | standard |
|---|---|---|---|
| Publishers differ in whether they deposit ORCIDs | Matching on journal and month holds the publisher constant | Removed | S9 |
| OpenAlex infers ORCIDs | Primary exposure uses only publisher-authenticated ORCIDs | Removed | S3 |
| Journals changed ORCID policy over time | Matching on month; window from 2016 | Disclosed | |
| Paper mills may adapt by registering ORCIDs | Would bias toward the null; the result is a snapshot of a moving target | Disclosed | |

## 11. Probes

| probe | computes | goes to | what would change the design | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **PA** | share of cases and of controls whose Crossref record carries any author ORCID, marginally | 5 | under 30 percent of articles with any deposit makes the exposure mostly zero | not run |
| **PB** | case counts per reason class from 2016 | 5 | fewer than 300 honest-error cases makes the contrast imprecise | not run |
| **PC** | the author's 100 publisher-page checks | 8 | below 95 percent the exposure source changes | needs the author |

## 12. What this cannot show

- Whether requiring ORCIDs would prevent anything.
- Anything about fraud that has not been retracted.
